hints: The new label of a node depends only on when it is first discovered. What traversal decides the discovery order here, and how will you remember which old node got which new label?
Run a BFS from start, visiting neighbours in increasing label order, and keep a map old → new label (an int[] filled with -1 works). Also keep the list of old nodes in discovery order.

1. Set newId[start] = 0, add start to order.
  2. Walk order like a queue; for each node sort its neighbours.
  3. Give every unseen neighbour the next label and append it to order.
  4. Finally, for copy node i (old node order[i]), translate each neighbour through newId and sort.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: BFS once to assign labels, then translate every edge of the reachable part through the label map and sort each row.

explain: For adj=[[1,3],[0,2],[1,3],[0,2]], start=2: node 2 gets label 0. Its neighbours 1 and 3 get labels 1 and 2. From node 1 we find 0, which gets label 3. Now translate: copy node 0 (old 2) touches old 1,3 → [1,2]; copy node 1 (old 1) touches old 0,2 → [3,0] sorted [0,3]; and so on. Nodes not reachable from start never get a label and are not part of the copy.
recognize: Copy a graph while relabelling nodes in discovery order → BFS with an old→new id map.
